brief_problem: Three loops that change in one line

runs.text: If the only thing that changes between two loops is an operation, the operation can be a value.
The kiosk keeps its prices in a list:
. All three have the same walk and change in a single line.
How is the walk written only once?
Imagine the three programs side by side. Which line is different in each?
Only the one that computes the new price:
. Everything else, creating the new vector, walking and adding, is identical. If that line were a value, the walk would be written once.

entries.text: What goes in and what comes out?
The prices and the operation go in; a new vector with the changed prices comes out.
: walking, filtering and gathering, always with the same shape.
Which part is calculation and which part touches the world?
Everything is calculation: only showing the result touches the world.

blocks.description: The prices 3, 5 and 2 go through three machines, one per step. The first changes each one and gives 4, 6 and 3. The second is a gate that only lets the cheap ones through: 2. The third is a funnel that gathers them into a single value: 10.

caption.text: Three machines for collections: one changes each box, another lets some through and another gathers them all into a value.

points.text: A function can be passed as a value; a function that receives or gives back functions is higher-order.
Mapping applies a function to each element; filtering keeps the ones that meet a condition; reducing combines them all into a single value.
